newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss Banque Vaudoise profits up 8.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Swiss Banque Vaudoise profits up 8.3 pct.

text.p: Switzerland's fifth largest bank, Banque Cantonale Vaudoise, said on Tuesday net profits rose 8.3 percent to 90.5 million Swiss francs in 1996 when private banking and asset management were among the brightest spots of its business.

The Lausanne-based, 50 percent state-owned cantonal bank said Switzerland's economic weakness meant loans and client deposits grew only slowly in 1996, but revenues from asset management and foreign exchange were higher than expected.
At a news conference in Lausanne, the bank also said its dividend per bearer share, to be proposed to its annual shareholders meeting on May 14, would be unchanged from 1996 at 17.50 Swiss francs.

Ralph Ziegler, a member of the executive board in charge of international banking, said the bank forecast annual profits to grow steadily to between 120 and 150 million Swiss francs over the next 10 years but gave no figures for 1997 and 1998.

As part of a restructuring in the over-banked Swiss market, Banque Cantonale Vaudoise said it planned to axe some 100 jobs in 1997 to bring its workforce down to 1,900 by end-year and cut another 100 jobs in 1998.
It would also close down 10 branches in 1997 to bring the total number to 73 -- down from 120 in 1995.

Private banking, which bankers say is booming in Switzerland with assets growing at an estimated annual 15 percent or more on average, was one profitable area for the bank in 1996 although fee erosion was emerging as an issue because of competition.

Claude Courvoisier, the bank's director general in charge of finance, said private client assets in 1996 grew by 25 percent to some 17 billion Swiss francs out of 30 billion in total client assets including institutional ones.

Commission income and service fees in 1996 totalled 148 million Swiss francs and contributed to some 40 percent of total income, Courvoisier told Reuters, but refused to give a breakdown for private and institutional clients.
He said fee erosion was becoming a major issue for domestic banks in Switzerland because of competition and expected commission incomes to decline over the coming years.
The fastest growing market for the bank's private banking business was Asia, Courvoisier added.
